definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Breaker Block in Trading
what_it_says: Opening line: a breaker block is a failed order block that has flipped sides.
The breaker block idea comes from ICT (Inner Circle Trader); teachers do not all agree on the exact rules.
A bullish breaker block comes from a failed bearish order block (the last opposite candle before the impulsive move down) and acts as support on the retest; the bearish case is the mirror.
A liquidity sweep must come first in the ICT version; a broken order block with no sweep before it is called a mitigation block. Some SMC traders call any broken order block a breaker.
Failure is confirmed by a candle body close through the order block; a wick alone may be another sweep.
Breaker blocks often fail; marking one is subjective and easier in hindsight.
definition_sources.which_candle: the failed order-block candle itself (up-closing for a bullish breaker)
not_specified: how long to wait for the retest

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Breaker Block
what_it_says: A breaker block is an order block that failed and flipped roles.

Bullish case: price runs below a prior low, then reverses and breaks back above the swing high that preceded the run; the down-closing candle or series that drove the failed move lower is the breaker. FAQ: a bullish breaker is built from down-closing candles.

Two readings circulate: the strict one requires the failing swing to first trade beyond a prior high or low (that raid separates a breaker from a mitigation block); the looser one treats any violated order block as a breaker.
Marking conventions vary (bodies only or full range). Breakers do not always hold on the retest.
definition_sources.which_candle: down-closing candle or series inside the failed down-leg (for a bullish breaker)
not_specified: any lookback, threshold or waiting time

definition_sources.name: MQL5 blogs: Breaker Blocks: Why Most ICT Traders Draw Them Wrong (And the 3 Conditions That Make One Valid), by Diego Arribas Lopez
what_it_says: Bullish case: the bearish candle range that formed the original swing high is the breaker, marked from its high to its low.
Three conditions: a real liquidity sweep first, displacement through structure, a first retest.
Says the sweep condition alone eliminates most of what gets labelled a breaker.
definition_sources.which_candle: the bearish (down-closing) candle or candles that formed the swing high
definition_sources.caveat: The post promotes the author's paid MetaTrader indicators. It shows no win rate or backtest.
not_specified: numeric definition of the sweep or of displacement

origin_conclusion: TMGM's page says the idea comes from ICT. No dated primary source for when the term was first used was found.
